correctness.rationale: Reconstructed full state (16 binary cells, one position and one of four headings), update turn/flip/move and explicit inverse. Every state is cyclic because the finite update is a permutation. Independently enumerated all 4,194,304 states and 128 rule-preserving translations/D4 actions, with global board complement for orientation reversals; grouped all primitive cycles. Exact independently recomputed complete 25-row table: 46,976 primitive temporal cycles, 4,194,304 period-weighted states, 376 geometric classes, minimal period 16 (16,384 cycles), maximum period 512 (256 cycles, two classes). This is exhaustive integer enumeration for this finite object, not extrapolation to other torus sizes. Original C++ full-source certificates separately use orbit mapping and Burnside fixed-cycle sums.

evidence: 3x4 full source has 196,608 states, 2,480 temporal cycles and a 48-element symmetry group; 2xn formula covers width-two degenerate geometry rather than a 4x4 square. Twisted-torus complexity does not classify 4x4 primitive cycles.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Previous torus families and broad ant complexity/recurrence theorems address different geometries, so none mathematically specializes to these 4x4 period and group fixed-sum counts.

value.rationale: The 4x4 torus is the first nondegenerate even-even periodic square grid with four distinct cardinal neighbors. Its exact 25 clock lengths, sixteen-divisibility beyond the known general even-even eight-divisibility restriction, and nontrivial 376 orbit symmetry classes are a natural complete classification and reproducible benchmark for initial-condition sensitivity. A single motivated complete finite object is substantively useful even without an all-n formula.

limitations: An unindexed historical enumeration might contain the same finite 4x4 census.
Program-assisted exhaustive finite proof is not a theorem for any other torus size; independent enumeration validates only defined group and state encoding.
